raw_prompt: Build an export pipeline that strips 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor direct identifiers before analytics ingestion.

cumulative_requirements.title: Strip 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor Direct Identifiers
cumulative_requirements.description: The export pipeline must identify and remove or redact all 18 categories of direct identifiers specified under the HIPAA Safe Harbor method prior to analytics ingestion.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly and unambiguously stated in the user prompt.

cumulative_requirements.title: De-identification Validation and Audit Logging
cumulative_requirements.description: The pipeline must generate an immutable audit log recording the timestamp, record count processed, and verification status confirming the complete removal of the 18 Safe Harbor identifiers before downstream transmission.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Why 1: Regulatory frameworks require demonstrable proof of compliance to avoid severe HIPAA penalties for data leaks. -> Why 2: An automated validation step coupled with an audit log creates an unalterable trace of the de-identification process. -> Why 3: No dataset may be transmitted to analytics ingestion without programmatic proof of zero remaining direct identifiers.

cumulative_requirements.title: Analytics Ingestion Format Standard
cumulative_requirements.description: The precise serialization format, schema definitions, and ingestion protocol for the downstream analytics platform remain unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify the target analytics system type, schema requirements, or data transport protocols (e.g., Parquet, JSON, S3 bucket, Kafka stream).

cumulative_requirements.title: Source Data Store and Access Mechanism
cumulative_requirements.description: The source database technology, connection protocol, and extraction schedule for raw health data remain unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt mandates the transformation logic but does not define where the raw data originates or how it is accessed.

cumulative_requirements.title: Dates of Service Generalization / Shifting Invariant
cumulative_requirements.description: The pipeline must shift or truncate all ages over 89 and dates related to individuals (except year) to comply with HIPAA Safe Harbor date aggregation rules, preventing indirect re-identification through temporal precision.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: HIPAA Safe Harbor requires removing or generalizing explicit dates and ages over 89. Step 2: The Pass 1 requirements only cover the 18 direct identifiers but omit temporal attributes like exact timestamps and ages which act as quasi-identifiers. Step 3: Therefore, a specific transformation guard for dates and ages must be enforced to prevent structural non-compliance.

cumulative_requirements.title: Pipeline Failure Recovery and Partial Ingestion Poison Pill Protection
cumulative_requirements.description: The pipeline must implement atomic transaction boundaries and dead-letter queue (DLQ) routing for records failing de-identification parsing, ensuring malformed or non-compliant records never leak into the analytics store.
cumulative_requirements.provenance: Data Engineering and HIPAA Minimum Necessary Standard
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: Export pipelines processing sensitive health data encounter malformed records or parsing exceptions. Step 2: Unhandled exceptions during stripping can lead to partial flushes or unredacted payloads bypassing the audit step. Step 3: Hence, a robust failure isolation mechanism (DLQ/atomic rollback) is mandatory to guarantee zero unredacted leaks upon pipeline crashes.

cumulative_requirements.title: Downstream Re-identification Risk & Quasi-Identifier Constraint Check
cumulative_requirements.description: The pipeline must evaluate residual re-identification risk (e.g., k-anonymity checks) for rare demographic combinations even after the 18 direct identifiers are stripped.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: Safe Harbor mandates stripping 18 identifiers, but sparse combinations of remaining attributes can still uniquely identify individuals. Step 2: Relying solely on strict Safe Harbor stripping without verifying composite uniqueness leaves residual exposure to linkage attacks. Step 3: Therefore, a secondary safeguard validating quasi-identifier distribution is necessary for rigorous data protection.

cumulative_requirements.title: Graceful Shutdown and Power Loss State Recovery
cumulative_requirements.description: The export pipeline must handle sudden termination signals (SIGTERM, SIGINT) and power loss events by flushing in-flight buffers, rolling back uncommitted source extraction transactions, and persisting execution cursors to ensure at-least-once or exactly-once processing without duplicate ingestion or data corruption.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Ensures system resilience and prevents partial data writes or state loss during abrupt infrastructure scaling or maintenance cycles.

cumulative_requirements.title: Statutory Cryptographic In Transit and At Rest Boundary
cumulative_requirements.description: All data in transit across pipeline components and at rest in staging or dead-letter queues must be encrypted using FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptographic modules to maintain HIPAA Security Rule compliance.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Statutory mandate requiring technical safeguards for protected health information (PHI) regardless of pipeline deployment architecture.

cumulative_requirements.title: Unstated Cryptographic Tokenization Provider
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific identity provider, hashing salt rotation mechanism, or cryptographic tokenization engine used for pseudonymization or pseudonym mapping storage remains unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify how persistent pseudonyms or reversible/irreversible token maps are managed across pipeline runs.

cumulative_requirements.title: Unstated Network Transport and Messaging Protocol
cumulative_requirements.description: The underlying message broker, streaming framework (e.g., Apache Kafka, AWS Kinesis), or RPC protocol used between pipeline stages remains unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: No explicit architecture or transport protocol was mandated in the original prompt.
